question: During the Basic Control Skills test, what may happen if a driver opens the vehicle door while it is still moving (not in neutral and park)?
choice_a: It counts only as a free look
choice_b: Nothing, as long as the door is closed again quickly
choice_c: It results in a warning only, never a failure
choice_d: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
explanation: If a driver opens the door while the vehicle is in motion (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: On a bus, what counts as a 'look' if the driver walks to the back of the bus to get a better view?
choice_a: It counts as a "look"
choice_b: It does not count as anything
choice_c: It is only permitted during Straight-Line Backing
choice_d: It disqualifies the driver immediately
explanation: On a bus, if the driver walks to the back of the bus to get a better view, it counts as a "look."
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: How many free looks may a driver be allowed on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, and Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, respectively, to check the position of the vehicle?
choice_a: Two free looks on Exercise 2, and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_b: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
choice_c: A maximum of one free look on Exercise 2, and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_d: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
explanation: A driver may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: On which two exercises is the driver scored for the 'final position' of the vehicle?
choice_a: Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, and Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: All four exercises equally
choice_c: Exercise 1, Forward Stop, and Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking
choice_d: Only Exercise 1, Forward Stop
explanation: The driver is scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, and on Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: What happens if a driver does not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, within the final exercise boundaries?
choice_a: Only a verbal warning is given
choice_b: The driver will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
choice_c: The driver is simply given a free re-do of the exercise
choice_d: There is no penalty as long as the mirrors do not cross the boundary
explanation: If the driver does not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, the driver will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: What can happen if a driver fails to follow the examiner's instructions for completing a Basic Control Skills exercise as directed?
choice_a: The examiner completes the exercise for the driver
choice_b: It results in only a minor point deduction
choice_c: The exercise is simply repeated with no penalty
choice_d: It may result in an automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
explanation: Failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: Which of the following is given as an example of an 'unsafe act' that may cause automatic failure of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Sounding the horn when instructed to do so
choice_b: Taking a few extra seconds to complete an exercise
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake, or opening the door while in motion
choice_d: Asking the examiner for clarification of instructions
explanation: Committing an unsafe act -- such as forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion -- may result in automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Scoring

question: In Exercise 1, Forward Stop, how many times may the driver stop the vehicle while driving forward through the alley?
choice_a: Twice, with one free stop
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: Up to three times
choice_d: As many times as needed
explanation: In Exercise 1, the driver drives forward through the alley and stops with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end without going past it; the driver may stop only once.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1 Forward Stop

question: After stopping in Exercise 1, Forward Stop, what must the driver do before the examiner will score the exercise?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
choice_b: Turn off the headlights
choice_c: Wait without moving until told otherwise, with no other action
choice_d: Immediately exit the vehicle
explanation: When stopped in Exercise 1, the driver must set the parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn; the examiner will then score the exercise.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1 Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, how far must the driver back the vehicle?
choice_a: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
choice_b: Only halfway through the alley
choice_c: Backward and then forward again in a zigzag pattern
choice_d: In a full circle back to the starting point
explanation: In Exercise 2, the driver backs straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing

question: What is the driver scored on during Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Fuel efficiency
choice_b: Speed only
choice_c: Use of turn signals only
choice_d: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
explanation: The driver will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position during Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing

question: During Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits (to check around the vehicle) is the driver allowed?
choice_a: Unlimited free pull-ups and exits
choice_b: No free pull-ups or exits at all
choice_c: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_d: One free pull-up, and the driver may safely exit the vehicle only one time
explanation: The driver is allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing

question: What must the driver do during Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Back the vehicle through a narrow alley
choice_b: Drive forward and steer left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line
choice_c: Parallel park between two cones
choice_d: Complete a full U-turn within the exercise boundaries
explanation: In Exercise 3, the driver demonstrates the ability to maneuver around objects while moving forward, driving forward and steering left through the opening into the opposite lane while keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking

question: During Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking, are free back-ups allowed, and may the driver exit the vehicle?
choice_a: Two free back-ups are allowed, and the driver may exit once
choice_b: Unlimited back-ups are allowed
choice_c: There are no free back-ups, and the driver is not permitted to exit the vehicle
choice_d: The driver must exit the vehicle partway through the exercise
explanation: In Exercise 3, there are NO free back-ups, and the driver is NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking

question: What is the driver scored on during Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Final position only
choice_b: Time taken to complete the exercise
choice_c: Back-ups, encroachments, and forward tracking clearance
choice_d: Use of the horn
explanation: The driver will be scored for back-ups, encroachments, and forward tracking clearance -- keeping the rear tire between the cone and the line -- during Exercise 3.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, how close to the rear of the alley must the rear most part of the vehicle come?
choice_a: It must touch the rear boundary exactly
choice_b: Within ten feet
choice_c: Within one foot
choice_d: Within three feet
explanation: In Exercise 4, the driver offset backs into the alley, bringing the rear most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box at the end.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_b: Two free pull-ups, and the driver may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times
choice_c: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_d: No free pull-ups are allowed
explanation: The driver is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must a driver pass before proceeding to the Road Test?
choice_a: A written essay about driving safety
choice_b: The Basic Control Skills test
choice_c: A separate hazmat test regardless of cargo carried
choice_d: There is no prerequisite for the Road Test
explanation: The manual states that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 12, Road Test

question: During the On-road Driving test, which of the following must the driver do at all times?
choice_a: Drive as fast as safely possible to show confidence
choice_b: Keep only one hand on the wheel at all times
choice_c: Wear a safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_d: Avoid using turn signals unless requested by the examiner
explanation: During the test, the driver must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, what may the examiner ask the driver to do?
choice_a: Simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing if in that situation
choice_b: Drive to another location to find the situation
choice_c: Skip that portion of the test entirely with no scoring
choice_d: Automatically fail that section of the test
explanation: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the driver may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing if they were in that traffic situation.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: What is considered 'unsafe coasting' while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Braking well before reaching the turn
choice_b: Using the turn signal too early
choice_c: Slowing down smoothly while changing gears
choice_d: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear -- clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral -- for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: As a driver approaches an intersection, what should they do if it is necessary to come to a complete stop behind a stop sign or signal?
choice_a: Coast to a gradual stop to save brake wear
choice_b: Come to a complete stop with no coasting, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front, and the vehicle must not roll forward or backward
choice_c: Stop as close as possible to the vehicle ahead to save space
choice_d: Roll slowly forward until traffic clears
explanation: If necessary, the driver must come to a complete stop, with no coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front, and the vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what must the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Decelerating and yielding to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Checking traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_d: Keeping both hands on the wheel
explanation: When driving through an intersection, the driver must check traffic thoroughly, decelerate and yield to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection, and must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the road test, where should the driver's vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Straddling two lanes for better visibility
choice_b: In the center turn lane at all times
choice_c: As far left as possible to avoid parked cars
choice_d: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit
explanation: During the urban business portion, the driver's vehicle should be centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: What must a driver do before changing lanes during the multiple lane portion of the road test?
choice_a: Change lanes as quickly as possible to minimize time in the blind spot
choice_b: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so
choice_c: Signal only after starting to move into the new lane
choice_d: Change lanes without signaling if no other cars are visible
explanation: During lane changes, the driver should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.4, Lane Changes

question: What must a driver do before entering an expressway or rural/limited access highway?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop at the merge point
choice_b: Accelerate to maximum speed before checking mirrors
choice_c: Wait for a signal light before entering
choice_d: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
explanation: Before entering the expressway, the driver should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the stop/start maneuver, once the vehicle is stopped, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately exit the vehicle to inspect it
choice_b: Leave the vehicle in drive with a foot on the brake
choice_c: Leave the turn signal on and keep the engine in gear
choice_d: Cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, and apply the parking brake
explanation: Once stopped for this maneuver, the vehicle should be parallel to the curb or shoulder and safely out of the traffic flow; the driver should cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve during the on-road test, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Brake hard only once fully inside the curve
choice_c: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_d: Shift gears in the middle of the curve for better control
explanation: Before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve, and should keep the vehicle in the lane.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.7, Curve

topic: Railroad Crossing: General Rule for All Drivers
question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must all commercial drivers avoid doing?
choice_a: Decelerating and braking smoothly before the crossing
choice_b: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_c: Checking traffic in all directions before reaching the crossing
choice_d: Looking and listening for the presence of trains
explanation: Before reaching a railroad crossing, all commercial drivers should decelerate and brake smoothly, look and listen for trains, and check traffic; they must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: If driving a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, within what distance from the nearest rail must the driver stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: At least 500 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: There is no specified distance
choice_d: Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
explanation: The driver of a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, then look and listen in both directions for an approaching train.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify?
choice_a: The color of the overpass
choice_b: The name of the road below
choice_c: The posted clearance or height
choice_d: The manufacturer of the overpass
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after going over a bridge, the driver may be asked about the posted weight limit.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.9, Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: During the student discharge exercise on the road test, how far from students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 50 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: There is no set distance during this exercise
choice_d: Exactly 2 feet
explanation: As the driver stops for the student discharge, the school bus must come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop, then place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: If a manual transmission is unsynchronized, what technique must the driver use when shifting?
choice_a: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_b: Shift without using the clutch at all
choice_c: Ride the clutch continuously between gears
choice_d: Rev the engine heavily before every shift
explanation: If equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting, and should not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which of the following clutch habits is the driver scored against during the road test?
choice_a: Fully releasing the clutch after each shift
choice_b: Riding the clutch, coasting with the clutch depressed, or 'popping' the clutch
choice_c: Double-clutching on an unsynchronized transmission
choice_d: Using the clutch to start the vehicle from a stop
explanation: The driver should always use the clutch to shift, but should not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or 'pop' the clutch.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Regarding gear usage, when should a driver avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: Before coming to a complete stop
choice_b: In turns and intersections
choice_c: On straight, empty roads
choice_d: There is no restriction on where to shift
explanation: The driver should not grind or clash gears, should select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine, and should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.12(b), Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What braking habits is a driver scored against during the road test?
choice_a: Applying steady, smooth brake pressure
choice_b: Braking early before a stop sign
choice_c: Coming to a complete stop at a stop line
choice_d: Riding or pumping the brake, and braking harshly instead of smoothly
explanation: The driver should not ride or pump the brake, and should not brake harshly, instead braking smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.13(c), Brake Usage

question: On a multiple lane road, in which lane should a driver finish a left turn, and which lane should a right turn finish in?
choice_a: Both turns may finish in any lane on the roadway
choice_b: A left turn should finish in the far left lane regardless of the center line
choice_c: Both turns must finish in the right-most (curb) lane
choice_d: A left turn should finish in the lane directly to the right of the center line; a right turn should finish in the right-most (curb) lane
explanation: Under lane usage rules, the driver should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, finishing a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line, and finishing a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017), Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- Section 13.1.14(d), Lane Usage
